answers.evidence:
Reproduced the flake with **real measured timings**, not fabricated values:

- **Natural rate:** `TestMeasureDistribution` (4000 real executions of `Execute` under a 20ms deadline, 64 workers) measured `min = 19.83ms`, with 0.03–0.42% of samples under the 20ms nominal — exactly the under-nominal class that breaks `>= 20ms`.
- **Deterministic reproduction:** widened the preemption window with an explicit `runtime.Gosched()` between deadline arming and `start` capture (the identical descheduling the OS scheduler does naturally). Across 4000 real samples: `min = 19.92ms`, **37 samples (0.9%) rejected by the old `>= 20ms` predicate, 0 rejected by the new 15ms–500ms band** (`TestCompareAssertionsUnderLoad`).
- **Stability:** fixed test run 19,200 executions (`-parallel=64 -count=300`) and 3,200 more with `-race` — zero failures. The old assertion passed only because 25,600 uncontended runs here didn't hit a sub-nominal sample; on contended CI hosts at 0.03–0.4%/run it fails within hours, matching the ticket.

Edge cases tested (all pass):

| Case | Old assertion | New band |
|---|---|---|
| Flake value 19.7ms (exact FLAKE-001) | **FAIL** | pass |
| Nominal 20.0ms / comfortable 21ms | pass | pass |
| Way-short 5ms (broken truncation) | fail | **fail** (lower bound catches) |
| Full 1s sleep (not truncated) | pass | **fail** (upper bound catches) |
| ctx already canceled | n/a | pass (immediate return, `context.Canceled`) |
| `-short` mode | n/a | heavy probes skip cleanly |
| `-race -parallel=64` | flaky | pass |

Also verified: `go vet` clean; deterministic predicate simulator (`TestTimeoutAssertionBand`) locks in the band semantics forever, independent of wall-clock luck.
